#### §31: Utilities

| ID | Spec | Ann. | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| D-31.1 | §31 | — | **The utilities are spec §31 with their own decision series D-31 and view `s31` (UTIL-0; `plan/utilities.md` Q7, owner's approval 2026-11-14).** §31 specifies what callers depend on (command names and paths, options, output formats, exit codes, files read and written, environment) for ldconfig, ldd, getent, getconf, iconv, locale, localedef, zic, zdump, tzselect, gencat and pldd, and what is not provided (§31.14); each item cites POSIX, a man page, RFC 8536, Appendix D, or a case of `spec/behaviour/utilities.glibc.txt` (black-box probe `tools/probe/util_spec.sh`, run as an ordinary user on the reference). A behaviour the design decided differently is marked **Liella rule**, with a differences row and a D-31 decision. Tooling: `cargo xtask stubs` reads the sections after §30 (§30, the pattern catalogue, gives no clauses: `spec::NO_CLAUSES`), so §31's clauses are `s31_<sub>_<field>_<n>` and their stubs are `crates/core/tests/s31_utilities_clauses.rs`; `spec/schedule.tsv` gives §31 to the track `UTIL` (from VAL, started 2026-11-14), so each UTIL story specifies its clauses in place. |
| D-31.2 | §31 | — | **Shape of the utilities: a library per domain holding both sides of each file format, one executable per domain, ldconfig freestanding and static (`plan/utilities.md` §3-§4, Q1 and Q2; owner's approval 2026-11-14).** Each format's writer lives in the crate of its reader (the loader cache in `liella-ld`, TZif in a `liella-tz` crate shared with the C library's reader, locales in a `liella-locale` crate, catalogs beside `catopen`'s reader), so reader and writer are tested against each other. `liella-tz` answers as zic, zdump and tzselect and `liella-locale` as locale, localedef, locale-gen, update-locale and validlocale, chosen by `argv[0]`; a domain with one command is a plain program. ldconfig is a freestanding static program with no C library dependency (dpkg needs it before any package operation and while `libc6` is replaced); Liella's `libc-bin` declares interest in the dpkg `ldconfig` trigger. UTIL-SHAPE measures the domain executables against separate programs (start-up instructions, faults, size); a domain that costs more falls back to separate programs (a build change only). Public interfaces: the commands and the file formats; a public Rust `tz` API in `liella-native` after UTIL-10 (UTIL-16); a `locale` API deferred; no new C ABI until a C consumer asks (D-X.10). |
| D-31.3 | §31, App. D | — | **On-disk formats stay compatible (owner's ruling 2026-11-14).** The utilities write TZif per RFC 8536 (zic, §31.9), the loader cache in the Appendix D.3.1 new format with the D.3.2 extensions (ldconfig, §31.2), the locale directory and archive of D.1 (localedef, §31.8), and the catalog format of D.2 (gencat, §31.12), so files written by Liella's tools and by the reference's are interchangeable, and coexistence systems and direct readers keep working. A Liella-native format (for example for the CLDR-derived locale set) is proposed only with a measured gain and a decision of its own. |
| D-31.4 | §31.1, §31.2 | — | **Identity strings of the utilities are Liella's (`plan/utilities.md` Q3; owner's approval 2026-11-14).** The first line of `--version` is `<command> (Liella <version>) 2.39`, the bug-report line of `--help` names Liella's channel, and ldconfig's tag 0 text (`Cache generated by:` in `-p`) names Liella's ldconfig; the trailing ABI level `2.39` stays, so scripts that read the version number see the ABI they get. No compatibility option: the banner states who built the program, and a script that tells C libraries apart (for example by `ldd --version`) must see the truth. The mirror scan of LIELLA-SYSTEM-LIBC-PLAN counts scripts that match the reference's banner text before UTIL-3 ships; a match it finds is raised with the owner. The transcript harness (UTIL-1) masks identity strings when it compares. `getconf GNU_LIBC_VERSION` follows `confstr` (§24), not this decision. |
| D-31.5 | §31.14 | — | **Not installed: `iconvconfig`, `/etc/bindresvport.blacklist`, `sprof`, `sotruss`, `mtrace`, `nscd` (`plan/utilities.md` Q4, owner's approval 2026-11-14; R8).** `iconvconfig` indexes conversion modules and Liella has none (D-6.8: charsets are built in or read from the installed charmaps); `/etc/bindresvport.blacklist` serves Sun RPC, which Liella does not implement; the `libc-devtools` commands have no caller in the caller search of the design; `nscd` is dropped (R8; Liella's name-service cache is in the library, D-16.10). No compatibility option: there is nothing for a restored command to act on. Revisited if the mirror scan of LIELLA-SYSTEM-LIBC-PLAN finds callers. gencat and pldd are kept (UTIL-14, UTIL-15). |
| D-31.6 | §31.2 | — | **`ldconfig -c old` and `-c compat` are refused (`plan/utilities.md` Q5, owner's approval 2026-11-14; #941).** ldconfig prints a message naming the new format as the one it writes and exits nonzero without writing anything; `-c new` (the default) is accepted. No compatibility option: Liella's loader reads only the new format (D-27.16, #941), so an old-format cache would be ignored by the loader it serves. The reference writes the old format on request (probe `ldconfig-c-old`). |
| D-31.7 | §31.3 | SEC | **ldd never runs the operand's code or another interpreter (`plan/utilities.md` Q6, owner's approval 2026-11-14).** ldd lists each operand through Liella's loader in list mode (`--list`, D-27.16), which maps the dependencies and runs none of their code, so ldd and the loader agree on every resolution. For an operand whose `PT_INTERP` is not Liella's loader, ldd lists by Liella's rules and says so on standard error. So ldd on an untrusted file runs none of its code. No compatibility option: running an untrusted file's code is the behaviour this rule exists to remove. `-v` reads the version needs itself. `-d`, `-r` and `-u` need relocation processing, so they are refused with a message until DL-10. |
| D-31.8 | §31.14 | — | **The `locales` commands are Liella's own (`plan/utilities.md` Q8, owner's approval 2026-11-14; R1).** `locale-gen`, `update-locale` and `validlocale` are reimplemented inside `liella-locale` from their man pages (locale-gen(8), update-locale(8)) and the files they use (`/etc/locale.gen`, `/etc/default/locale`, `SUPPORTED`); they compile in process, one parse of each charmap and shared source for all requested locales, in parallel. Counters per locale against one `localedef` process per locale decide any speed claim (UTIL-13). Their interface clauses are added with UTIL-13. |
| D-31.9 | §31.2 | SEC | **ldconfig writes a deterministic cache, replaces it atomically, and treats every file it reads as untrusted (`plan/utilities.md` §4; owner's approval 2026-11-14).** Entries are in the Appendix D.3.3 order, ties broken by configuration order and then path bytes, and directory listings are sorted, so identical trees give byte-identical caches on any file system. The cache is written to a temporary file in its own directory, synced, and renamed over the old one. Every ELF file is bounds-checked and never mapped executable. `-r ROOT` resolves every path inside ROOT with `openat2(RESOLVE_IN_ROOT)` and needs no privilege (the reference also succeeds for an ordinary user, probe `ldconfig-r-user`); `chroot` only where `openat2` is missing. An auxiliary cache (under `/var/cache/ldconfig/`, Liella's own file) only if UTIL-3's counters show a gain. |
